title: Quantum Entropy Contraction and Factorization from Hypercontractivity
abstract: We prove that hypercontractivity implies entropy contraction for a single quantum channel, without a detailed balance condition. For primitive quantum Markov semigroups that are KMS-symmetric with respect to a faithful invariant state \(σ\), we obtain the modified Log-Sobolev bound $α_1\geq \fracλ{(2+\log\|σ^{-1}\|_\infty)}$ where $λ$ is the spectral gap. This removes the assumption of \(L_p\)-regularity for the comparison through the log-Sobolev constant. As an application, we show that the hypercontractivity of an average of two conditional expectations implies the approximate tensorization of relative entropy.

bite.hook: We prove that hypercontractivity implies entropy contraction for a single quantum channel without detailed balance.
tldr: Proved that hypercontractivity implies entropy contraction for a single quantum channel without needing detailed balance.
Obtained a modified Log-Sobolev bound for primitive quantum Markov semigroups.
Showed that hypercontractivity of an average of two conditional expectations implies approximate tensorization of relative entropy.
bite.whyItMatters: Entropy and information bounds are vital for quantum information theory. Removing strict assumptions like detailed balance expands how we analyze quantum channels.
bite.eli5: Entropy measures how mixed up or chaotic things are. Researchers found a mathematical rule that proves how information spreads out and calms down in quantum systems under broader conditions than before.
